summary: Granite Cave capture Bite was submitted twice across commit/verify
symptom: A single committed Bite was observed first at 27 -> 10 HP, then the verification phase advanced another Bite and fainted the wild Aron.

unexpected.predicted: One Bite would be nonlethal under the modeled 17-22 damage interval and leave Aron available for a ball after verification.
unexpected.actual: The commit returned Aron at 10/27 and PP 24, while subsequent verification reported another Bite and Aron fainted; final Grotle Bite PP was 23.
diff: one requested move produced two PP decrements
wild target fainted despite the first observed HP being nonzero

authority.oracle: live RAM plus drained battle text

reproduction.observed: single requested action crossed an unstable queued-action boundary

hypotheses: commit's choose_move returned before the queued action fully resolved
verify treated a still-live command/menu marker as permission to advance another action

root_cause.claim: the commit/verify acknowledgement contract is not stable at command-menu return
evidence: PP 25 -> 24 at commit, then 24 -> 23 during verify
first post-commit target HP was 10, final text reported a second Bite

solution.contract_change: Do not use game_battle_commit followed immediately by game_battle_verify until a stable post-action boundary is implemented and regression-tested.
solution.workaround: Use one direct state-controller action, wait for drained battle text and stable HP/PP/species across two observations, then evaluate the next action.

domain_knowledge: A nonlethal normal-damage estimate is not sufficient if a transaction can submit twice.
regression_cases: wild Aron 304 at 27/27, Grotle 388 Bite slot 0 at command menu
tooling_contracts: A command-menu observation is provisional until post-action HP/PP/species and feedback are stable.

action_changing_unknowns: whether commit or verify owns queued action resolution
next_experiments: test a single direct controller action with explicit stable-boundary polling
add a regression test before promoting a transaction fix
